data.narrative:
Hermeus, a Series C supersonic and hypersonic propulsion company founded by AJ Piplica, Skyler Shuford, Glenn Case, and Mike Smayda, is currently valued at $1.0B post-money on $500M raised. The sector remains sparsely populated with limited public and private comparables—two public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and one private peer (Boom Supersonic)—making traditional peer-median analysis unreliable.

Given the narrow comp universe, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology applied to the $1.0B Series C post-money. A 1.7x step-up multiplier, typical for Series C to next-stage advancement, implies a forward valuation of $1.7B. This approach directly anchors to Hermeus' own transaction history without forcing extrapolation from incomparable peers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B, centered on $1.7B. The range reflects reasonable variance around stage-progression estimates but remains narrow given reliance on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of aerospace capital cycles, regulatory pathways for hypersonic vehicle certification, and the durability of any near-term technical advantages. The scarcity of sector comparables limits external validation and suggests heightened dependency on bottom-up operational and market assumptions not captured in valuation mechanics alone.
